claims.text: Introducing tungsten interlayers into HEA multilayers will mediate the transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
Tungsten interlayers will maintain coherent or semi-coherent interfaces in HEA multilayers.
Coherent or semi-coherent tungsten interfaces reduce atomic diffusivity.
Coherent or semi-coherent tungsten interfaces allow dislocation nucleation under increased stress.
The initial HEA multilayer coatings have as-deposited coherent interfaces.
Changing tungsten interlayer thickness by sputter deposition modifies interface coherency.
Both diffusion-controlled and dislocation-controlled creep mechanisms can be activated under the proposed high-temperature, high-stress conditions.
Tungsten has a high melting point.
Tungsten has low diffusivity under the relevant creep conditions.
Tungsten's high melting point and low diffusivity stabilize the multilayer interface.
The tungsten interface limits excessive diffusion at lower stresses or temperatures.
Limiting diffusion delays diffusion-mediated creep.
At higher stress, a coherent tungsten interface facilitates dislocation nucleation and motion.
Tungsten-interlayered HEA multilayers will show reduced diffusion creep at lower stresses relative to the control.
Tungsten-interlayered HEA multilayers will undergo a controlled transition to dislocation-mediated creep at higher stresses.
The tungsten interlayers will improve the creep resistance of the HEA multilayer system.
HEA multilayers without tungsten lack a tailored interface capable of controlling the creep-mechanism transition.
The proposed effect occurs only within a particular range of tungsten interlayer thicknesses.
Tungsten interlayers that are too thin may be ineffective.
Tungsten interlayers that are too thick may cause interface incoherency or brittleness.
